source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: Form 4884 Section D line 19 (PDF page 22 Line 19: up to 98,846 joint; PDF page 20 'Recipients born during the period from January 2, 1959 through December 31, 1966'); Worksheet 3.3 lines 1-6 (PDF page 25: total public and private benefits against one limit); Schedule 1 line 27; MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = spouse 1 Michigan public pension 60,000.00 + spouse 2 IRA distribution 50,000.00 + interest 4,150.00 = 114,150.00. Federal taxable income = 114,150.00 - federal standard deduction (31,500.00) = 82,650.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan (older spouse born 1961: Section D; public benefits are not unlimited in this branch): Worksheet 3.3 line 1 131,794.00; line 2 0.00; line 3 131,794.00; line 4 x 75% = 98,845.50, which the form (whole dollars) and line 19 give as 98,846; line 5 public 60,000.00 + private (IRA after 59 1/2) 50,000.00 = 110,000.00; line 6 smaller 98,846.00 to Schedule 1 line 27. Line 14 = 114,150.00 - 98,846.00 = 15,304.00; exemptions 2 x 5,800 = 11,600.00; line 16 = 3,704.00. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 3,704.00 x 0.0425 = 157.42. No credits; state income tax 157.42.
